name: mab-bernoulli
description: Classical MAB: 10 Bernoulli instances with 10 arms (means uniform in [0.05, 0.95], gap >= 0.05), 2 runs each. Theoretical defaults.

notices.title: Default hyperparameters
notices.text: Some policies use the values from their papers: alpha=1 for UCB1, UCB1Tuned, UCBV and UCBMinV1; c=3 for KLUCB. These values are safe in theory. In practice, they often explore too much. The regret can then be higher than with tuned values.
notices.todo: Search the best values with param_grid=True. Or set them yourself, e.g. UCB1(alpha=0.1).

notices.title: Not stored
notices.text: This run does not store the per-action estimates and the action of every step. The charts cannot show them.
notices.default: Regret, reward, CPU time and wall time only (track=(), measure_memory=False).

notices.title: Curves stored every 50 steps
notices.text: The curves keep one value every 50 steps. Between two kept steps, the line is drawn, not measured. You set log_interval=50.
notices.todo: Set log_interval=1 to keep every step. The files get larger.

notices.title: Slower timings
notices.text: Peak memory is measured (measure_memory=True). This makes Python code about 5 times slower. So the CPU times are higher than in a normal run.
notices.todo: Set measure_memory=False for normal CPU times. Compare CPU times only between runs with the same setting.
